l4_steps.name: Define commission tier structure by agency segment
l4_steps.input: Historical agency booking data, competitive intelligence, budget guidance
l4_steps.output: Draft commission tier matrix segmented by agency type and channel
l4_steps.kpi: Commission cost as % of total distribution revenue ≤3.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Legacy GDS commission structures limit dynamic per-segment tier adjustments; IATA Resolution 818 constrains net-rate transparency, reducing ability to differentiate incentive rates by booking window or route

l4_steps.name: Model financial impact of proposed commission rates
l4_steps.input: Draft commission tier matrix, O&D revenue data from Amadeus NRM
l4_steps.output: Financial impact model with revenue-at-risk analysis and break-even volumes
l4_steps.kpi: Commission ROI ≥4:1 incremental revenue per dollar paid
l4_steps.pain_point: Incomplete NDC booking attribution in data lake distorts channel profitability calculations — NDC and GDS bookings not tagged consistently in Redshift, leading to underestimation of NDC cost savings

l4_steps.name: File commission schedules in ATPCO CAT 35
l4_steps.input: Approved commission tier matrix from budget sign-off
l4_steps.output: Published ATPCO CAT 35 commission schedules distributed to all GDS platforms
l4_steps.kpi: Filing cycle completed ≤2 business days from policy approval; zero GDS distribution failures
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO CAT 35 supports net fares rather than explicit commission rates, requiring workaround constructions that reduce transparency for agency partners and complicate audits under IATA Resolution 850

l4_steps.name: Validate IATA/ARC accreditation for new agency
l4_steps.input: New agency onboarding request with IATA/ARC number
l4_steps.output: Accreditation verification record; agency status confirmed as current and bonded
l4_steps.kpi: Onboarding validation completed within 3 business days of request submission
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA accreditation lapses and bond failures are not automatically propagated to GDS agency profiles — risk of continuing commission payments to deaccredited agencies discovered only at BSP settlement

l4_steps.name: Configure commission parameters in GDS platforms
l4_steps.input: Validated accreditation record, approved commission tier assignment
l4_steps.output: Agency commission profile active and consistent across Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS
l4_steps.kpi: Configuration accuracy 100%; zero commission miscalculation incidents per quarter across all three GDS platforms
l4_steps.pain_point: Managing parallel commission configurations across Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus requires manual triple-entry with no centralised commission API — errors typically discovered only at monthly BSP/ARC settlement, creating retroactive adjustment workload

l4_steps.name: Enroll agency in NDC incentive programme
l4_steps.input: Agency NDC API certification status, signed NDC incentive agreement
l4_steps.output: Agency NDC incentive profile active; incremental booking targets and incentive rates configured
l4_steps.kpi: NDC share of enrolled agency bookings ≥15% within 90 days of enrolment
l4_steps.pain_point: Many TMCs and leisure agencies lack technical capability for full NDC API integration; incentive uptake is constrained by agency IT readiness rather than demand, reducing the effectiveness of shift-to-NDC distribution strategy

l4_steps.name: Extract historical agency performance data
l4_steps.input: 24-month GDS MIDT data, NDC booking events, agency tier classification history
l4_steps.output: Agency performance scorecards: revenue contribution, yield, load factor uplift by route
l4_steps.kpi: Data extraction latency ≤4 hours for full 24-month dataset; completeness ≥99% of expected agency records
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS MIDT data arrives with 24–48hr delay and does not distinguish flown versus unflown bookings at ingestion — performance scorecards overstate agency contribution until cancellation netting is applied in a separate downstream process

l4_steps.name: Set incentive thresholds and tier boundaries
l4_steps.input: Agency performance scorecards, annual incentive budget allocation from Finance
l4_steps.output: Incentive programme terms sheet: booking thresholds, earning rates, measurement period, eligible routes
l4_steps.kpi: Target incentive budget utilisation ≥85% by end of programme period; zero over-budget accruals
l4_steps.pain_point: Revenue Management incentive budget inputs are static annual figures — no dynamic recalculation when O&D demand shifts mid-year, causing misalignment between incentive thresholds and actual revenue opportunity by quarter

l4_steps.name: Approve override rates for strategic partner accounts
l4_steps.input: Incentive terms sheet, strategic partner account plans, revenue policy guardrail limits
l4_steps.output: Signed incentive agreement with approved override commission rates; uploaded to SAP contract management
l4_steps.kpi: Override approval cycle ≤5 business days of proposal submission; 100% of overrides documented with ROI justification
l4_steps.pain_point: Override approvals require VP-level sign-off but historically tracked in email threads with no structured workflow — creates audit exposure under IATA Resolution 850 and SOX internal controls for airline revenue contracts

l4_steps.name: Ingest daily booking volumes from GDS and NDC
l4_steps.input: Sabre MIDT, Amadeus MIDT, Travelport MIDT feeds, NDC API booking event stream
l4_steps.output: Daily agency booking volume dashboard; commission accrual staging table updated
l4_steps.kpi: MIDT ingestion completeness ≥98% of expected records per day; ingestion pipeline latency ≤6 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: MIDT data does not distinguish flown versus unflown bookings at time of ingestion — commission accruals include no-show and subsequently cancelled bookings that must net out at BSP settlement, creating transient overstatement of liability

l4_steps.name: Calculate commission accruals against tier thresholds
l4_steps.input: Daily booking volume data, approved tier thresholds and override rate agreements
l4_steps.output: Commission accrual journal entries posted to SAP GL; agency tier status report
l4_steps.kpi: Accrual calculation cycle completed within 2 hours of MIDT ingestion; accrual variance to final settlement ≤1%
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP accrual entries require manual journal adjustment when an agency crosses a tier boundary mid-month — automated tier-crossing triggers not yet configured, exposing the process to under-accrual risk and period-end restatements

l4_steps.name: Flag agencies approaching performance thresholds
l4_steps.input: Daily accrual report, tier threshold proximity rules (within 10% of next tier)
l4_steps.output: Account management action list; proactive outreach triggers for agents within reach of next incentive tier
l4_steps.kpi: ≥90% of threshold-proximity alerts actioned within 48 hours; conversion rate of nudged agencies reaching next tier ≥35%
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated CRM integration between Tableau alerts and account management workflows — alerts require manual transfer, causing follow-up delays that reduce the effectiveness of incentive tier nudging as a revenue acceleration tactic

l4_steps.name: Generate commission billing statement via BSP/ARC
l4_steps.input: Final monthly accrual report, confirmed flown-only booking data after cancellation netting
l4_steps.output: Commission billing statement; BSP debit memo or ARC IAR report
l4_steps.kpi: BSP/ARC billing statement issued within 5 business days of month-end close; billing accuracy vs accruals within ±2% tolerance
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP remittance data format (IATA Resolution 850) does not map directly to SAP GL coding — manual field-by-field rekeying required, creating a 2–3 day reconciliation lag and introducing transcription error risk at scale

l4_steps.name: Post commission payables to SAP AP
l4_steps.input: Validated BSP/ARC billing statement reconciled to accruals
l4_steps.output: Posted AP invoice; payment run scheduled in SAP; GL entries aligned to accrual period
l4_steps.kpi: AP posting completed within 2 business days of billing statement validation; on-time payment rate ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-currency commission payments (USD, EUR, GBP) require FX conversion at time of AP posting — exchange rate movement between accrual date and payment date creates untracked P&L exposure not captured in current distribution cost reporting

l4_steps.name: Process and resolve agency dispute claims
l4_steps.input: Agency dispute submission referencing original booking data and billing statement line items
l4_steps.output: Dispute resolution decision; adjusted credit note issued via BSP Link if claim upheld
l4_steps.kpi: Dispute resolution cycle ≤15 business days; dispute rate ≤2% of total monthly invoices by value
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA BSP dispute window is 12 months — historical disputes can surface against already-closed SAP accounting periods, requiring prior-period adjustment journals that breach internal month-end close policies and trigger external audit queries

l4_steps.name: Analyse commission ROI by channel and agency segment
l4_steps.input: Full-year commission payments from SAP, channel revenue data from Amadeus NRM, per-booking cost by channel
l4_steps.output: Commission effectiveness report with channel ROI ranking, cost-per-booking comparison GDS vs NDC, and under/over-performing agency list
l4_steps.kpi: Incremental revenue per £1 commission paid ≥4:1; NDC cost-per-booking ≤60% of equivalent GDS cost
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC and GDS bookings are not comparable on a per-booking-cost basis without blended modelling spanning GDS segment fees, NDC API development costs, and commission payments — data lives across Redshift, SAP FI, and GDS billing portals with no single unified view

l4_steps.name: Revise commission tier structure for next programme cycle
l4_steps.input: Commission effectiveness report, Finance budget guidance for next period, Legal sign-off on rate changes
l4_steps.output: Revised commission tier matrix approved; ATPCO CAT 35 filing initiated for next programme period
l4_steps.kpi: Policy revision cycle completed ≤30 days before new programme period start; zero ATPCO filing errors on submission
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO filing lead time for commission changes is 7–14 days — late budget approvals from Finance regularly compress the filing window, risking programme launch delays that disrupt agency booking behaviour during high-demand booking periods
